summary: Steel fire tower on Weed Patch Hill in Brown County State Park, Indiana; built about 1927 (sources differ), used for park visitors and radio, standing; NHLR-registered January 2026 with a restoration fundraising drive.

access.note: Observation tower in a state park that visitors can reach. The cab is not open, and no official rule on climbing was found.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1928 report gives eighty feet (24.4 m), which matches the record. The Register gives 90 to 100 feet and a November 1941 newspaper item gives 90 feet. Sources disagree; the record keeps 24.4 m as the as-built figure.

The 1928 report and a July 1927 photo point to 1927, and the Register says circa 1927. The plan report is dated 1926 by the Register and hobby site but 1923 by a Forest Lookouts transcription. The wooden sign at the site says the 1930s. Sources disagree; 1927 has the most support.

notes_for_editor: Build year is 1927 by the 1928 report (quoted by NHLR) and a July 1927 photo; the sign says the 1930s. The plan report that announced the tower is dated 1926 by the Register and hobby site but 1923 by the Forest Lookouts transcription; the story reports both. Height is 80 ft as built per the 1928 report, but the Register and a 1941 item say 90 ft or more; the record's 24.4 m is kept but may be revisited. Climbing: the hobby site says the cab is not open and the tower can be climbed partway; no official rule found, so the story does not encourage climbing. The 1944 staffing and radio items come from a Brown County Democrat clipping transcribed on the Forest Lookouts page; the clipping itself was not read. Restoration status: fundraising announced January 2026; no evidence of work started. Agency: Indiana DNR per NHLR; the Forest Lookouts header uses the older Department of Conservation name. Fire history: no specific fires found.
